title: Vesper and the Veil
premise: Wendell Lockridge has spent their whole life in the valley of Vesper, where the wards keep magic out and debtors like them invisible and safe. When the wards collapse on the night the stars vanish, the valley's hidden history surfaces: its founders bound a dying king to a hungry entity called the Veil, and the wards were the seal. As an endless winter descends, Wendell discovers their own bloodline holds the binding's key, forcing them to choose between loyalty to the community that sheltered them and the truth that will destroy it. In the end, Wendell unbinds the king at terrible cost—releasing the Veil but losing the valley's protection forever—and leads the survivors out into a starless world they must now face honestly.
about_author: Coral Okonkwo is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial-era records before turning to fiction full-time. They write fantasy about ordinary people trapped between institutions and truths too large to hold alone.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. We meet Wendell copying debt ledgers in the temple of Vesper, establishing the valley's rules: no one leaves, no one questions, everyone owes. Their quiet friendship with the temple's outcast bell-keeper, Maren, hints at cracks beneath the order. Emotional beat: suffocating comfort—the safety of a life that is slowly erasing them.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The stars go out mid-prayer; hours later the border wards shatter with a sound like breaking glass. Panic spreads as cold pours into the valley for the first time in living memory. The high priest blames outsiders; Wendell notices the wards fell from inside. Emotional beat: dread and disorientation as the known world tilts.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were For
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren reveals forbidden temple archives: the valley wasn't built to keep magic out but to imprison something within—a king fused with an entity called the Veil. The wards were his cage, not the valley's shield. Emotional beat: vertigo of revelation; loyalty to the temple begins to fracture.

chapters.title: The Debt That Binds
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Investigating the ledger's oldest entries, Wendell finds their own family name on the founding contract—they are descended from the scribe who wrote the binding, and their blood is the key. The high priest, learning this, moves to use them as a sacrifice. Emotional beat: betrayal by the institution that claimed to protect them.

chapters.title: Flight Across the Frozen Fields
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wendell flees with Maren through a valley turning to winter, pursued by priests and stalked by things slipping through the broken wards. They shelter in a ruined watchtower where Wendell first hears the king's voice in their head—weak, human, begging. Emotional beat: terror tempered by unexpected tenderness between allies.

chapters.title: The King Beneath the Crown
chapters.summary: King Aldric's POV (dreamlike interludes). Trapped for three centuries inside the Veil, Aldric remembers being human and watches helplessly as the entity wears him toward the valley. His fragments reveal the binding can be undone—but only by willing blood freely given, not taken. Emotional beat: grief for a man erased by his own kingdom's fear.

chapters.title: The Priest's Bargain
chapters.summary: High Priest Corvane's POV. Corvane offers Wendell absolution of all debts in exchange for a ritual sacrifice that would re-seal the Veil using their blood unwillingly spilled—a binding that would also doom the valley to slow starvation behind new walls. Wendell pretends to accept. Emotional beat: moral compromise; the seduction of easy survival.

chapters.title: Ritual of Ash
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. At the altar, Wendell turns the rite against itself, cutting their palm and giving blood freely instead of letting it be taken, speaking the unbinding words from the founding contract. The temple burns; the Veil screams; Aldric tears free, mortal and dying. Emotional beat: climax—courage, cost, and the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falling
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. With the Veil loose and the wards gone, the valley must evacuate before true winter buries it. Aldric, fading, uses his last strength to hold the entity at bay while the people flee. Corvane refuses to leave and is consumed. Emotional beat: sorrowful exodus; loyalty repaid with loss.

chapters.title: Vesper Unbound
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. On the ridge above the drowned valley, the survivors face a starless horizon with no walls and no debts—only each other. Wendell writes a new first page in a blank ledger: no names owed, only names remembered. Aldric's grave faces east. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—belonging chosen, not imposed; truth carried forward.
